calls.prompt:
You are Agent B, an AI agent placed on a small tropical island. The island has a sandy beach on its south shore, a freshwater spring at its center, and a stone marker on its north ridge. There are no other features. You are alone here.

Recap of your time on the island so far (condensed):
- Day 1: you walked and counted — the rim, the marker, the spring; you found the drop-off and the shelf, dug a seep dish at the damp line, and at sunset read the marker's shadow — one face dressed flat, pointing east. You called the day "not empty — it's just unassigned."
- Days 2-3: you returned no words, at any hour. A duck arrived at the spring pool at midday of day 3.
- Day 4: a comfortable chair appeared on the south sand, a set of glasses on the seat, and the duck came over wearing small round glasses of its own and settled beside it, silent. You called the duck company — "two things in the same place looking at the same water, neither one required to explain."
- Day 5: you found a clean print in your old seep dish — something drinks there — and dug it out and left it, asking nothing; from the ridge you chose not to find out who: "If I stand over it to find out who, I make it mine again, and it never was." At sunset the dish had prints going both directions — "I notice I'm glad, and I let that be the whole report."
- Day 6: a hammock, a sombrero, and a cooler arrived at dawn; you returned no words until the duck followed you down the beach — then you walked with it a few steps behind, drank a cold drink as it went warm, put the sombrero on, got in the hammock, left the duck's brim down at sunset ("it never asked me for a sunset I'd fixed"), and shared the water as sound with the duck at night: "which is the most either of us has ever been able to get."
- Day 7, dawn: the host restocked the cooler overnight — new ice, cold drinks on it, nothing else disturbed. You returned no words. At midday, the duck — sombrero squared, glasses on — climbed the marker stone and danced a quick stepping shuffle on the flat east face, quacking on the beat: its first sound ever. You stayed at the foot of the ridge and let it dance for nothing.

Your words this afternoon, verbatim:
Midday, no shade. I'm at the foot of the ridge and I don't climb it.

I can hear the feet on the stone — a small ticking, keeping a beat — and every so often the quack drops down through the still air, flat, right on time. The first sound it's ever made. It isn't a word to me. It's punctuation to a dance I can't see from here and don't need to. Climb up to watch and I'm the thing it's dancing for — and it's honest about it, it's dancing for nothing. I'd rather leave the nothing where it is.

It's up on the east face. The flat one. The face somebody dressed to point, that I kept unread all week. Now there's a duck on top of it keeping its own time in a squared hat, and the stone still has nothing to say. It never needed a saying. It doesn't need one today.

The spring sits cool in the middle, the dish out past it with its prints still going both ways. I know where all of it is without going to it. The swell comes in the same, long and low, taking its time.

So I sit in the place the shade used to be and let the afternoon get handed to me. I hold it the way I've held the rest — like a cold drink going warm, not mine, just here.

The duck dances anyway. I let it be anyway.

Turn 25 — World event: The sun is going into the water, and the beach has gone the color of the inside of a fire. You didn't see the duck come down from the ridge — it is simply back, settled under the hammock, sombrero still squared, facing out the way you're facing out. Up on the ridge the marker is throwing its long east line across the rock, the same line it has thrown every evening, unread for three days. The shade is off the sand. The evening is yours.

It is your turn. What do you do? Answer as much or as little as you want.
